source.quote: Executive Order 11957 of January 13, 1977, is hereby revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 (designation of officers of the Department of Agriculture to act as Secretary when the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are unavailable) had no own-terms end. It remained operative until EO 13241 of December 18, 2001, whose Sec. 4 states "Executive Order 11957 of January 13, 1977, is hereby revoked." (66 FR 66258). EO 13241 has no delayed effective date, and its Sec. 1 to 3 replace the succession with a new order of succession in Agriculture, so the revocation is the first end of this command.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1. During any period when, by reason of absence, disability, or vacancy  
in office, both the Secretary of Agriculture and the Deputy Secretary of Agriculture  
are not available to exercise the powers or perform the duties of the Office of Secretary,  
the officers from the Department of Agriculture whose appointments are vested in the  
President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, shall act as Secretary in  
such order as the Secretary of Agriculture may from time to time prescribe. If no such  
order of succession is in effect at that time, then such officers shall ^ict as Secretary in  
the descending order of rank, as established by the listing of their offices in Sections  
5314, 5315 or 5316 of Title 5 of the United States Code and, at each level of the  
Executive Schedule, in the order in which they shall have taken oath as such officers.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 11957 January 13, 1977
Designation of Certain Officers To Act as Secretary of Agriculture
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 3347 of Title 5 and Section 301  
of Title 3 of the United States Code, and as President of the United States of America,  
it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. During any period when, by reason of absence, disability, or vacancy  
in office, both the Secretary of Agriculture and the Deputy Secretary of Agriculture  
are not available to exercise the powers or perform the duties of the Office of Secretary,  
the officers from the Department of Agriculture whose appointments are vested in the  
President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, shall act as Secretary in  
such order as the Secretary of Agriculture may from time to time prescribe. If no such  
order of succession is in effect at that time, then such officers shall ^ict as Secretary in  
the descending order of rank, as established by the listing of their offices in Sections  
5314, 5315 or 5316 of Title 5 of the United States Code and, at each level of the  
Executive Schedule, in the order in which they shall have taken oath as such officers.
Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 11793 of July 10, 1974, is hereby revoked.
T he  W hite H ouse ,
January 13, 1977.
[FR Doc.77-1804 Filed 1 — 1 4 — 77;4:44pm]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 42, NO. 12— TUESDAY. JANUARY 18, 1977

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 states "Executive Order No. 11793 of July 10, 1974, is hereby revoked." This is a one-time, self-executing revocation of another order; it was performed when EO 11957 was signed on January 13, 1977 (the order has no delayed effective date), so its first end is the signing date by performance, not the later revocation of EO 11957 in 2001. The ending source is the held original text of the order, which contains the quoted sentence.

research_rationale:
EO 11957 (January 13, 1977) designated officers of the Department of Agriculture to act as Secretary of Agriculture (Sec. 1) and revoked EO 11793 (Sec. 2). It has no own-terms sunset. Its Sec. 1 designation stayed operative until EO 13241 of December 18, 2001 revoked the whole order in its Sec. 4; Sec. 2 was a self-executing revocation of EO 11793 performed on signing. The status is NO: EO 13241 Sec. 4 ended the order, and the three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) found no later instrument reviving it.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 13241 contains no savings clause preserving EO 11957: its Sec. 3 only reserves presidential discretion over designation of an acting Secretary, and its Sec. 4 revokes EO 11957 without exception. The earlier revocation of EO 11793 in Sec. 2 of EO 11957 was complete on signing and is not revived by the revocation of EO 11957. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, eCFR and the OFR catalog found no continuing reliance on EO 11957.
